title: The Farewell Wine Murder Case
notes: Recurring detective-cast nodes (Kogoro Mouri, Conan) omitted by convention; Ran is kept only implicitly via the video-tape mechanic and otherwise not separately tracked. This case has a genuine, strongly-modeled red herring: Kazue really did inject a vintage wine bottle with a muscle relaxant intending to kill her father, and is caught doing so on-screen -- but Ichikawa secretly never drank it (he poured it into a flowerpot to test his daughters), so her attempt, while real, is not what killed him. The actual cause of death is Dr. Okano's openly-administered 'heart stimulant' injection, which was really the poison, exploiting Ichikawa's own faked-collapse test and his position as trusted physician. case_type: murder.

clues.desc: The wine glass shows no sign Ichikawa actually drank from it, and a nearby flowerpot smells of wine -- proving he secretly discarded the poisoned wine Kazue prepared for him instead of drinking it, which means something other than the wine must have actually killed him.

The hidden camera Ichikawa installed to test his daughters instead recorded his own death: Dr. Okano openly giving him an injection everyone assumed was a heart stimulant, at the exact moment his staged collapse was meant to happen.
